definition: Data made of pairs of values: two measurements taken from each member of a sample, such as the age and price of each car.
A graph that plots each pair of bivariate data as one point, with one variable on each axis.
How closely the points of a scatter diagram follow a straight line, and whether that line slopes up (positive) or down (negative).
The number $r$, with $-1 \le r \le 1$, that measures the strength and direction of the linear correlation between two variables.
The value that $\lvert r\rvert$ must exceed, for a given number of data pairs, before the linear correlation counts as significant rather than possibly due to chance.
The point $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ made from the mean of the $x$ values and the mean of the $y$ values; lines of best fit and regression lines pass through it.
A straight line drawn by eye through the mean point of a scatter diagram, following the trend of the points.
A link in which a change in one variable directly produces a change in another.
The straight line fitted to bivariate data by least squares; the line of $y$ on $x$, $y = ax + b$, makes the squared vertical distances as small as possible and is used to predict $y$ from $x$.
Using a model to predict a value for an $x$ inside the range of the data the model was built from.
Using a model to predict a value for an $x$ outside the range of the data the model was built from, which may be unreliable.
